episodes.153867: One of the most significant flooding events in years occurred during November 11th and 12th, given both the amounts of rainfall and the footprint where flooding occurred.  In the wake of high pressure passing east off the mid-Atlantic coast, a plume of deep tropical moisture was rapidly carried inland to the central Appalachians ahead of a slow-moving cold front.  Though this plume was of tropical origin, it was not directly related to Tropical Storm Eta, which was off the coast of southern Florida.  Precipitable Water values were in the extremely high range of 1.9 to 2.2 inches with this airmass, around the 99th percentile for mid-November.  In addition, evapotranspiration was significantly lower than during the previous few months given lower daytime heating and the fact that most vegetation had become dormant for the upcoming winter months.  Despite dry conditions for almost two weeks leading up to the event, numerous instances of flooding and flash flooding occurred as 4 to 6 inches of rain fell across portions of the Piedmont on the 11th, followed by an additional 1 to 3 inches on the 12th.  Some of the activity was convective in nature, producing locally 2 to 4 inch per hour rainfall rates.  The rainfall produces numerous instances of flooding and flash flooding, followed shortly by river flooding.
episodes.154105: Moisture from Tropical Storm Eta was drawn northward into the Mid Atlantic during the day of Wednesday November 11th. Meanwhile, a slow moving cold front approached the area and made its way through central North Carolina during the day Thursday, resulting in widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms. Rainfall totals were generally in the 4 to 6 inches range, although some spots near Rocky Mount saw close to 10 inches of rain by the time the event drew to a close. This resulted in numerous flooded road, including one death resulting from the flash flooding. One thunderstorm also caused some localized storm damage in Sampson County.
episodes.154480: Tropical Cyclone Eta moved from the eastern Gulf of Mexico, across the northern Florida peninsula, to off the South Carolina coast throughout the 11th and 12th. Tropical moisture streaming into the Carolinas throughout this time resulted in development of heavy rainfall, with widespread rainfall amounts of 4 to 6 inches, with locally higher amounts across the foothills and Piedmont of North Carolina. This resulted in areas of flash flooding and main stem river flooding, some of which was significant, resulting in multiple fatalities and significant damage.
episodes.154519: Tropical Cyclone Eta moved from the eastern Gulf of Mexico, across the northern Florida peninsula, to off the South Carolina coast throughout the 11th and 12th. Tropical moisture streaming into the Carolina Piedmont throughout this time resulted in development of heavy rainfall, with widespread rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches resulting in areas of flash flooding across York County.

events.narrative: Although heavy rainfall tapered off across Rowan County during the afternoon and evening, elevated flow conditions and some flooding persisted across many of the larger basins in the city through much of the evening. Numerous roads remained closed during this time.

Flooding briefly developed along Wildcat Creek and other streams in York County after runoff from 3 to 5 inches of rain that fell throughout the 12th resulted in gradual stream rises. McConnells Highway was inundated as was Saluda Rd near Highway 324 (due to Fishing Creek).
Flash flooding was reported along Justice Branch Road near Beaverdam Road.

Although heavy rainfall tapered off across the Catawba River basin during the afternoon and evening of the 12th, high water levels and elevated stream flows persisted in the area around Lookout Shoals dam during the overnight hours until the early morning of the 13th.
Flash flooding was reported near State Route 1924, near Turkey.

The Dan River at Paces, VA (PCEV2) was above flood stage (22 feet) from November 12th through the 15th and crested at the minor flood stage of 28.65 feet (47,000 cfs) at 4:15 PM EST on November 14th.  This was just over a 25-year Average Return Interval per the USGS StreamStats website.

Moderate flooding developed along the South Yadkin River after 4 to 6 inches on rain fell within the basin in less than 24 hours. Multiple roads were inundated on the Davie County side while several homes in the Cooleemee community were flooded.

Moderate flooding developed along the South Yadkin River after 4 to 6 inches on rain fell within the basin in less than 24 hours. Multiple roads were inundated on the Rowan  County side, especially in the upper reaches of High Rock Lake, where some campgrounds were also inundated.

The Dan River at South Boston (SBNV2) crested at 29.44 feet on November 15th at 1:15 am EST, which is the 14th-highest crest on record, but below two other crests that occurred earlier in 2020.  Flooding of this magnitude is between a 5- and 10-year event per USGS StreamStats.  Flooding from the Dan River caused water to flood the road and businesses along Highway 501 as far south as the intersection with Highway 58, about a half mile from the river.  The intersection was closed from late afternoon of the 14th until late afternoon of the 15th, when the river was around a stage of 28 feet.  Highway 501 remained closed until the morning of the 16th.
